> How a layer plays its samples, including granular synthesis and looping

The _PLAYBACK_ tab controls how the layer plays its Instrument's samples: straight through, rebuilt into textures by the [granular engine](#granular-synthesis), or [looping](#looping) for as long as you hold a note.

![A layer's PLAYBACK tab with its parts numbered](https://assets.floe.audio/website/screenshots/layer-playback.306deb78b66d7fc2.png)12345

1.  **Play mode** — there are three modes:
    -   _Standard Playback_ plays each sample straight through (or [loops](#looping) part of it).
    -   _Granular Playback_ uses [granular synthesis](#granular-synthesis), with the point the grains come from moving through the sample at a speed you choose (and looping, if a loop is set).
    -   _Granular Fixed_ also uses granular synthesis, with the point the grains come from set directly by a _Position_ control rather than moving on its own.
2.  **Waveform display** — for a single-sample Instrument, this is the sample itself. A multi-sampled Instrument contains many samples, so this shows the one from the most recent note (or a representative one until you play). If notes change too quickly to follow, it pauses on a recent sample, shown with a checkered overlay. When you play, red markers track each voice through the sample. The waveform often has [looping](#looping) controls as well.
    -   **Sample start** — the arrow on the bottom edge of the waveform sets where playback begins. Drag it to skip the beginning of the sound; the skipped part is shaded. If you move it into the audio, a few milliseconds of _Attack_ on the [volume envelope](/docs/beta/usage/main-tab#volume-envelope) avoids clicks. It isn't available for sliced Instruments.
3.  **Sample info** — shows whether the Instrument is a single sample or a multisample, with details such as the number of samples, or a single sample's length and root key.
4.  **Reverse** — play the samples backwards. It works in every play mode, with or without looping. The waveform flips to match, so playback always runs from left to right.
5.  **Loop mode** — choose how the sound loops, if at all. For example, you can use the Instrument's built-in loops, or set your own loop points on the waveform. Hover over the selector to see what the current setting does for this Instrument, and why some options may be unavailable.

Floe comes with a few simple built-in waveforms (oscillators). Many of the controls above don't apply to them, and so are hidden. Since they're algorithmic waveforms, the red voice markers are placed left to right by pitch instead of moving through a sample.

## Granular synthesis

As well as playing samples the usual way, from start to finish, each layer can switch to the granular engine. Granular synthesis plays lots of small snippets of the sample, called grains. Each grain can come from a different part of the sample, and play in a different direction, at a different pitch, or from a different place in the stereo field. It can completely transform a sample.

It's particularly good at smooth, lush textures. You can isolate a tiny fraction of a sample, such as one particular tonal moment, and hold it for as long as you like by running lots of grains over it. It's just as good at crackly, gritty textures, or at sparse ones where the grains are spread out so you can hear each one coming from a different point in the sample.

The granular engine works with any sampled Instrument. For each note, the grains come from the sample that note would normally play.

Granular synthesis uses randomness to keep the grains spontaneous and natural-sounding, rather than a mechanical, machine-gun-like repetition. Because of that, the sound can vary from note to note. When you want the same result every time, you have full control over that too: see [Reproducibility](/docs/beta/usage/reproducibility).

### The two granular modes

Choose a granular mode from the play mode menu at the top of the tab, where _Standard Playback_ is the usual way of playing samples.

-   **Granular Playback** — the point the grains come from travels through the sample at a steady speed, set by _Speed_. Use it to slow a sample down or speed it up without changing its pitch. It's not as precise as a dedicated time-stretching algorithm, but it gives a grainy or lush kind of time-stretch that's useful in its own right. Turn _Speed_ right down and the playhead barely moves, so a sample only a couple of seconds long can give you a whole minute of slowly changing texture. _Speed_ at 100%, the centre of the knob, is the sample's original speed, and the playhead still follows the sample start, looping and _Reverse_ settings.
-   **Granular Fixed** — instead of _Speed_ there's a _Position_ knob, which picks a precise point in the sample for all the grains to come from. _Spread_ sets how wide that region is.

Apart from _Speed_ and _Position_, the two modes have exactly the same controls.

### Getting started

Granular Fixed is perhaps the best place to start, because you can see and hear exactly what each control does.

![A layer's PLAYBACK tab in Granular Fixed mode with its parts numbered](https://assets.floe.audio/website/screenshots/layer-playback-granular-fixed.2140192424972f7d.png)123456

1.  **Share grains** — how grains build up when you play several notes at once.
2.  **Variation** — take the element of chance out of the grains.
3.  **Waveform display** — shows where the grains come from.
4.  **Playhead** — where in the sample the grains come from.
5.  **Grains** — the shape of each grain, and how much they overlap.
6.  **Random** — how much each grain differs from the next.

Choose _Granular Fixed_ from the play mode menu, then use _Position_ to pick the point in the sample you want to isolate. The highlighted region on the waveform shows where grains will come from. Play some keys: all the sound you hear is coming from that exact point, and lilac lines on the waveform show each grain as it plays.

From there, try these controls:

![The PLAYHEAD and GRAINS controls](https://assets.floe.audio/website/screenshots/granular-controls.9551a5fa66a30bfb.png)

-   **Density** — perhaps the next most useful control. It works a bit like an overlap percentage: at 0%, each grain starts as the previous one ends. Turn it up and new grains start sooner, so they overlap more and more, up to 100% where there may be hundreds of grains playing. Low values give an open texture where you can pick out individual grains; high values build a thick, continuous wash. High _Density_ uses more CPU.
-   **Length** — how long each grain lasts. Short grains chop the sound into a fine, buzzy texture; long grains keep much more of the sample's natural character. _Density_ and _Smooth_ are both measured relative to _Length_, so changing it changes how they feel too.
-   **Smooth** — how gently each grain fades in and out. High values give a softer texture, with neighbouring grains blending into each other. Low values make grains start and stop abruptly, for a grittier, glitchier texture.
-   **Spread** — widens the region that grains can come from, which you can see straight away on the waveform: each grain starts somewhere between _Position_ and a point this far past it. A narrow spread gives an isolated, pinpoint tone. Spread it out completely and grains come from all over the sample, for a texture that's much more varied, unexpected and full of different tones.

### Random

The controls under the _RANDOM_ heading (6) make the texture even more varied. Each grain picks its own settings at random as it starts, within the range you set. At 0% every grain is the same.

![The RANDOM controls and the Intervals menu](https://assets.floe.audio/website/screenshots/granular-random.2567c6ef69428431.png)

-   **Pan** — the higher it goes, the more likely grains are to be panned left and right. Especially with a high _Density_, it gives a rich stereo image, with grains spread right across it.
-   **Detune** — sets each grain's pitch at random, up to a semitone up or down. Low values give a chorus or unison-like thickness; high values sound obviously out of tune.
-   **Direction** — the chance of each grain playing in the opposite direction, backwards if the playhead is going forwards. At 100%, each grain is equally likely to play either way.
-   **Harmony** — the chance of a grain playing at a musical interval from the note you played. It works with the _Intervals_ menu beside it, and does nothing until you've chosen at least one interval there. For example, click _12_ in the menu's grid and some grains will play 12 semitones (an octave) above your note; turn up _Harmony_ and more of them will. Click a selected interval again to turn it off. You can pick lots of intervals at once, or choose a preset such as _Wide Octaves_, _Major Triad_ or _Pentatonic_. The note you played is always included. It's a great way to make lush, interesting tones.

![The open Intervals menu, with presets on the left and the grid of intervals on the right](https://assets.floe.audio/website/screenshots/granular-harmony.7692588f84b54478.png)

### Share grains

The button just to the right of the mode's name, showing a cloud of dots (1), chooses how grains build up when you play several notes at once. Hover over it to see which way it's set. It's there for both granular modes.

-   **Shared grains** — the number of grains stays the same however many notes you play. If you're after a sparse texture, it stays sparse even when you play a whole chord. Each grain plays from one of the held notes, so at a low _Density_ you can hear the grains hop between the notes of the chord. This is the default setting.
-   **Per-voice grains** — every note you play adds its own full set of grains. If your _Density_ setting gives 20 overlapping grains, a second note adds another 20, so the sound gets denser, and possibly louder, with each note.

### Variation

![The Variation and Seed settings, open beneath the Variation button](https://assets.floe.audio/website/screenshots/granular-variation.865ff2e8cbd88c95.png)

Each grain picks its starting point, pan, detune and so on at random, so every note you play scatters its grains differently. That keeps a granular sound alive, but it also means a pattern of grains you love might not come back. _Variation_ lets you make the grains the same every time instead.

Click the button (2), to the right of the share grains button, and choose one of these:

-   **Different on every note** (default) — every note scatters its grains differently. The best choice for most sounds, especially dense, textural ones. Even in this mode, you can get reproducible renders of your DAW track, see [Reproducibility](/docs/beta/usage/reproducibility).
-   **Identical on all notes** — every note plays exactly the same grains. Hold a chord and each note plays them at its own pitch. With shared grains, the notes take turns, so you hear the same grains come back at different pitches.
-   **Identical on each key** — each key gets its own pattern of grains. C3 always sounds the same, D3 always sounds the same (but is different to C3), etc..

With either _Identical_ option, the _Seed_ number picks which pattern repeats. Try a few numbers until you find one you like. It's saved with the preset, so the grains you chose are the grains everyone hears. The button lights up while one of the _Identical_ options is chosen.

See [Reproducibility](/docs/beta/usage/reproducibility) for more on seeds, and on making a whole performance come out the same every time in your DAW.

### Granular tips

-   In _Granular Fixed_ mode, the point the grains come from only moves when _Position_ does. To make it wander through the sample on its own, set the [LFO's](/docs/beta/usage/lfo-tab) target to _Grain Position_: the LFO sweeps _Position_ back and forth, so the texture keeps changing as you hold a note. Or link _Position_ to a [macro](/docs/beta/usage/macros) to move it by hand as you play.
-   The volume envelope, filter, EQ and effects all shape the granular sound just as they would in _Standard Playback_.
-   When designing a sound, try _Identical on all notes_ with a low _Density_ and step through a few _Seed_ values. Once you hear a grain scatter you like, save the preset and it's kept exactly.

## Looping

You can loop part of a sample for as long as you hold a note. Even a short sample can then sustain indefinitely, or you can pick out a section that has some movement in it, so the sound cycles through it over and over. You have full control over where the loop sits and how smoothly it joins up.

Looping works in _Standard Playback_ and in the _Granular Playback_ [granular mode](#granular-synthesis).

![A layer's waveform and loop controls with their parts numbered](https://assets.floe.audio/website/screenshots/looping.4f51878d98be7c61.png)123456

1.  **Loop start** — where the loop begins.
2.  **Loop end** — where the loop finishes, and playback goes back round.
3.  **Crossfade** — how smoothly the loop joins up.
4.  **Sample start** — where playback begins when you press a key. It isn't part of the loop, but it lives alongside it.
5.  **Reverse** — play the samples, and the loop, backwards. The loop end then appears on the left and the loop start on the right, though the loop points themselves don't change.
6.  **Loop mode** — how the sound loops, if at all.

### Loop modes

There are two modes of looping:

-   **Standard** — when playback reaches the loop end, it jumps back to the loop start, optionally smoothing the jump with a crossfade.
-   **Ping-pong** — uses the same start and end points, but at each end of the loop the playback direction reverses, so it goes back over what it just played, the other way.

Choose the loop mode from the selector (6). Which options are available depends on the Instrument. Some let you set your own loop points, some come with loops already built in, and some keep that control to themselves, such as sounds that are perfectly sustained or already loop.

![The loop mode menu](https://assets.floe.audio/website/screenshots/loop-mode-menu.96adc5ab47405221.png)

-   **Default** — let the Instrument decide: each sound loops, or doesn't, just as it was designed to. The menu shows what that means for the current Instrument.
-   **Built-in Loop - Standard** and **Built-in Loop - Ping-pong** — use the loop points that come built into the Instrument, looping in the direction you choose.
-   **No Loop** — each sound plays straight through.
-   **Custom Loop - Standard** and **Custom Loop - Ping-pong** — set your own loop points on the waveform.

Options that aren't available for the current Instrument are dimmed: hover over one to see why. Some Instruments have no built-in loops, for example, or don't allow custom loop points, or have sounds that must always loop. The selector itself shows what's actually happening, and hovering over it explains the current setting. The arrows beside it, and , step through only the options that are available.

### Setting your own loop

Choose one of the _Custom Loop_ modes, and the loop's handles appear on the waveform. Drag the loop start (1) and loop end (2) to set where the loop sits. The highlighted region between them is the part that loops. Drag inside the region to move the whole loop without changing its length.

The handles work like Floe's other [controls](/docs/beta/usage/controls): double-click one to type an exact value, `shift`\-drag for finer control, and `ctrl`/`cmd`\-click to reset it. Double-clicking the highlighted region types a value for the loop start.

For a multi-sampled Instrument, the loop points are positions through the sample, as a percentage of its length. Whichever sample a note triggers, it loops between those same percentages.

With a built-in loop on an Instrument that has just one sample, the handles show where the loop sits, but they're greyed out and can't be moved. To set your own, choose one of the _Custom Loop_ modes.

### Crossfade

A loop can click as playback jumps from one point in the sample to another. The crossfade (3) blends the audio across the join to smooth it out. A small crossfade usually helps, especially for sustained or tonal sounds. Drag its handle to change it.

-   In _Standard_ mode, the crossfade happens as playback nears the loop end, blending into the audio just before the loop start. Its handle sits inside the loop.
-   In _Ping-pong_ mode, the crossfade smooths each turnaround, blending in the audio just beyond the loop point. Its handle sits outside the loop.

The crossfade needs audio before the loop start to blend in from, so it can't be used while the loop starts at the very beginning of the sample: its handle is greyed out until you move the loop start later. The crossfade also has to fit within the loop and the sample, so it shrinks automatically if you make the loop too small for it. In _Ping-pong_ mode, it also needs room after the loop end.

### Looping tips

-   Looping needs the [volume envelope](/docs/beta/usage/main-tab#volume-envelope) to be on. With it off, nothing would ever bring a looping note to an end.
-   Pitch is changed by speeding up or slowing down playback. So the higher you play, the faster the loop cycles, and the lower you play, the slower. In _Granular Playback_ mode, the loop cycles at the rate set by _Speed_ instead.
-   In _Granular Fixed_ mode the grains always come from the _Position_ you choose, so there's no looping and the loop controls are hidden.
-   A loop can be moved by a [macro](/docs/beta/usage/macros). The highlighted region then shows where the loop actually is, while the handles stay at their own settings.

-   Release samples, which some Instruments play when you let go of a key, never loop.

---

# Randomisation

> Use an element of chance to find sounds you might not have found yourself

Floe has a few features that bring in an element of chance. It's a way to find spontaneous inspiration, and sounds you might not have reached for yourself. They're also good fun.

As with anything left to chance, sometimes the results are great and sometimes they're a bit too wacky. The _Undo_ button in the top panel is always available.

All of these randomisation buttons use the same shuffle icon, so you can identify them at a glance.

## Random variation

The main random feature is the _Random Variation_ strip on the [_Perform_](/docs/beta/usage/perform) page. It takes the preset you've loaded and changes some of its properties, giving you a fresh take on the sound.

![The Random Variation strip on the Perform page](https://assets.floe.audio/website/screenshots/perform-variation-strip.68e36d0f47412a76.png)

Click anywhere on the strip. Where you click sets how far the variation strays from the preset. Towards the left, the changes are mostly subtle and the sound keeps its character. Move towards the right to venture into wilder changes. As you hover, the strip shows the amount and a word for it, from _small variation_ to _extreme variation_.

The button at the left of the strip rolls another variation at the same amount as last time, so you can try several takes at an intensity you like.

Every variation starts from the preset as you loaded it, not from the previous variation, so you can keep clicking without drifting ever further away. When you find one you like, save it as a preset. That keeps it, and makes it the new starting point for further variations.

If nothing is loaded, the strip builds a random sound instead, around an Instrument picked at random.

### What a variation changes

A variation reworks the preset rather than starting from scratch, so it usually keeps something of the original's feel. Depending on how far right you click, it may:

-   **Swap Instruments** — each layer can get a different Instrument. Further left, the new one is usually a close relative, from the same library or folder or with similar tags. Further right, it can come from anywhere. With more than one layer in use, one is sometimes left as it is. Layers using a built-in waveform are never changed.
-   **Fill or empty layers** — an empty layer may get an Instrument, and occasionally a layer is cleared. Filling is much more likely than emptying, so wilder variations tend to add to the sound rather than thin it out. At least one layer always keeps an Instrument.
-   **Move the macros** — some of the preset's [macros](/docs/beta/usage/macros) are turned by a noticeable amount, taking everything they control with them.
-   **Change the effects** — some effects' mix levels move, and a few effects are switched on or off. An effect that's switched on gets fresh settings, kept within sensible limits so it won't suddenly jump in level.
-   **Shift octaves** — now and then, a layer's _Transpose_ moves up or down an octave or two.

## Jumping to a random item in a browser

Wherever you can choose a preset, an Instrument or an impulse response, there's a button that jumps to a random one:

-   **Presets** — in the top panel, next to the preset name.
-   **Instruments** — in each layer's header on the [_Layers_](/docs/beta/usage/layers#layer-header) page. It loads a random Instrument into that layer only.
-   **Impulse responses** — on the [Convolution Reverb](/docs/beta/usage/effects#convolution-reverb) effect.

Each button is linked to its [browser](/docs/beta/usage/browsers): it only picks from what that browser's filters allow, so you can set the bounds of what "random" means. Filter the preset browser to one library and a tag such as _ambient_, say, then keep clicking to jump around within that selection. The same goes for the browser's own button while it's open.

## Layers and effects

The button at the top right of the [_Layers_](/docs/beta/usage/layers) page loads a random Instrument into all three layers at once, as if you'd clicked each layer's button in turn. Each layer has its own Instrument browser filters, so narrow the first layer to bass sounds and the second to textures, for example, then click it to roll through combinations that stay within those bounds.

The button at the top right of the [_Effects_](/docs/beta/usage/effects) page randomly puts each effect in or takes it out of the rack, and shuffles their order. It leaves each effect's settings alone, so anything you've dialled in is still there when the effect comes back.

## Randomness in the sound itself

Parts of the audio engine, such as the [granular engine](/docs/beta/usage/playback-tab#granular-synthesis), also use randomness while you play, to create varied, natural-sounding performances. See [Reproducibility](/docs/beta/usage/reproducibility).

---

# Reproducibility

> How to make Floe's playback exactly reproducible in a DAW

Some features, most noticeably granular synthesis and the random LFO shapes, are designed around randomness to make the sound more natural and lively. Normally you don't need to worry about reproducibility: Floe's default setting, _Reset on transport_, covers most uses by making every render of your track in your DAW come out exactly the same. But sometimes those choices aren't quite what you want, such as grains landing in the wrong places or a random LFO moving the wrong way at a key moment. For that, Floe has _seed_ settings that let you take more control.

To understand what a seed does, it helps to know that Floe's randomness isn't truly random. It comes from a sequence of numbers that looks random. The sequence is so long that it never comes round again in practice, but it's fixed: from the same starting point, it always unfolds the same way. The seed is that starting point. So you keep all the spontaneity of random choices, but the same seed always gives the same choices.

Floe goes back to the start of the seed's sequence only at certain moments, called resets. You choose when they happen, and which seed to use, on the _Reproducibility_ tab of the [Performance Controls](/docs/beta/usage/performance-controls) panel:

![Reproducibility tab of the Performance Controls panel, with its settings numbered](https://assets.floe.audio/website/screenshots/reproducibility.acda98d8ce410fef.png)123

1.  **Reset on transport** — reset whenever you press play or start a render in your DAW. Play your track from the top twice and you hear exactly the same thing both times. It's on by default.
2.  **Reset keyswitch** — reset whenever Floe receives the MIDI note you choose here. Put that note in your MIDI just before a section, and that section plays back identically every time, wherever you start playback from. The keyswitch note makes no sound, and it's shown as a blue marker on the on-screen keyboard.
3.  **Seed** — which sequence Floe starts from. Change it to hear a different take, just as lively as the last and just as repeatable.

You can use either kind of reset, or both.

The _Seed_ also covers these smaller sources of variation:

-   The arpeggiator's _Humanise_ and random note orders

-   Which round robin sample plays first after a reset

-   The _White Noise_ Instruments

## Workflow

The _Seed_ settings are a finishing step. You choose a seed once your MIDI is recorded and you're getting ready to render, rather than while you're improvising.

There's one _Seed_ for the whole instance of Floe, and every random choice Floe makes moves its sequence along. So each choice affects all the choices that come after it. That's why it's important to ensure that you play the exact same notes with the exact same timing. A saved MIDI item in your DAW ensures this.

### With _Reset on transport_

This is the default. Floe starts from the _Seed_ whenever you press play or render, so everything from that point on comes out the same every time.

To judge a seed properly, render the whole track again, or play it from the very start. It won't sound the same if you start playback in the middle of a MIDI item, or between MIDI items played by the same instance of Floe, because Floe needs to make all the same choices from start to finish, not starting in the middle.

So the workflow is:

1.  Render your track, or play it from the very start.
2.  If something isn't quite right, change the _Seed_.
3.  Render again and listen, repeating until you have a take you like.

If Floe only plays in one part of your track, you don't need to go right back to the start. Anywhere before Floe's first note works just as well, since Floe hasn't made any choices before then.

### With _Reset keyswitch_

A _Reset keyswitch_ lets you lock in a performance with more granularity. Floe starts again from the _Seed_ every time the keyswitch note plays, so everything after it comes out the same no matter where you started playback or what Floe played before. You can add several of these lock-in points through your track, allowing you to audition the section after each one by starting playback just before its keyswitch.

This also suits looping a section: put the keyswitch at the start of the loop. A DAW loop jumping back to its start doesn't count as pressing play, so without the keyswitch each pass carries on from where the last one left off.

The catch is that every keyswitch uses the same _Seed_. If you change the seed to get a better take of one section, every other section that follows a keyswitch changes too. If a seed suits one section of your track but not another, load a second instance of Floe for that section and give it its own seed.

### Per-layer seeds instead

The [granular engine](/docs/beta/usage/playback-tab#variation) and the LFO's [random shapes](/docs/beta/usage/lfo-tab) offer an alternative to all of this: a per-layer seed , saved with the preset. Rather than waiting for a reset, it applies every time a note starts, so each note gets its own sequence. Choose one of the _Identical_ modes and try a few _Seed_ values until you like the result. It then sounds exactly the same on any computer, in any instance of Floe, without needing any of the settings above. Unlike the instance's _Seed_, it's a sound-design setting you can choose at any time.

## Tips

-   Floe can't recapture a variation after the fact. If an improvised take sounds great, the random choices behind it are gone. Record the MIDI first, then try seeds against it.
-   Performance Controls settings belong to the instance, so loading a preset leaves them untouched: you can try out presets without losing your seed and reset setup.
-   When designing a granular sound, try _Identical on all notes_ with a low _Density_ and step through a few _Seed_ values.

---

# Top Panel and Main Menu

> The top panel's preset box, buttons, master controls and meters, and everything in the main menu

The top panel runs along the top of Floe's window and stays there on every page. It holds the things that apply to the whole sound rather than to one page: the current preset, undo and redo, the master controls and the output meters, along with the buttons that open Floe's other windows.

![Floe's top panel with its parts numbered](https://assets.floe.audio/website/screenshots/top-panel-overview.6c17c53c76feceb5.png)12345

1.  **Logo and version** — the version of Floe you're running. If you turn on _Show instance name_ on the _General_ tab of Preferences, this instance's [name](/docs/beta/support/autosave#instance-names) appears after it.
2.  **Preset box** — the current preset's name and description, with buttons to step through presets, save, and load a preset from a file. Click the name to open the preset browser. See [The preset box](/docs/beta/presets/loading-presets#the-preset-box).
3.  **Buttons** — Preferences, Performance Controls, undo and redo, and the main menu.
4.  **Timbre and Volume** — the master controls, which act on everything you hear.
5.  **Meters** — the level of the final output.

## Buttons

-   **Preferences** — settings for Floe itself rather than for your sound, such as how the interface looks and where your sounds and presets are installed. They're saved on your computer and apply to every instance of Floe.
-   **Performance Controls** — how you play Floe: mostly MIDI settings, plus options for making performances exactly reproducible. They're saved with this instance in your DAW project, and loading a preset never changes them. See [Performance Controls](/docs/beta/usage/performance-controls).
-   **Undo** — step back through your changes to the sound, including tweaks to controls and loading Instruments or effects, so you can experiment freely. Hover over the button to see which change it will undo.
-   **Redo** — bring back a change you've just undone. If you make a new change instead, there's nothing left to redo.

-   **Attribution** — appears in red when a sound you've loaded comes from a library that asks to be credited. Click it for the exact text to use. See [Attribution](/docs/beta/reference/attribution).

-   **Main menu** — more options, and Floe's other windows. A red dot on the button means a new version of Floe is available: see [Updating](/docs/beta/installation/download-and-install-floe#updating).

## Master controls

-   **Volume** — the final stage of the sound. It comes after the [effects rack](/docs/beta/usage/effects), so it sets the overall level of everything just before the audio leaves Floe.

-   **Timbre** — some Instruments are built with crossfade layers: variations of the same sound, such as soft to hard or dark to bright. _Timbre_ sweeps between them, so you can shape the tone. While you drag it, the Instruments that respond are highlighted. When none of the loaded Instruments have crossfade layers, the knob is greyed out. An MPE controller can move it for each note separately: see [MIDI](/docs/beta/usage/midi#mpe).

## Meters

The peak meter (5) shows the level of the final output, measured after the master _Volume_. It flashes red if the signal clips above 0 dB.

There's also an optional loudness (LUFS) meter, mostly useful if you're making presets and want them to sit at a consistent level. Turn on _Show Loudness (LUFS) meter_ on the _General_ tab of Preferences, and hover over it for details.

## The main menu

Click , the last of the buttons (3), to open the main menu.

![Floe's main menu, open beneath its button in the top panel](https://assets.floe.audio/website/screenshots/main-menu.f549d251ee1a692d.png)

-   **Load Blank Preset** — return every setting to its default and clear all the Instruments and IRs, ready to build a sound from scratch. Remember, if you need it, _Undo_ brings back what you had.
-   **Panic (Stop All Sound)** — stop all audio and clear every playing note. Handy if a note gets stuck.
-   **Rescan Libraries & Presets** — Floe notices new and changed files in its folders by itself, but if something you've added doesn't show up, this makes it look through every folder again.
-   **Preferences** and **Performance Controls** — the same as the buttons in the top panel.
-   **Info** — the _Libraries_ tab shows what's installed and is where you can [uninstall](/docs/beta/installation/uninstalling) it. The other tabs show your version of Floe and whether an update is available, the legal notices, and some metrics, such as how many voices are playing and how much memory the samples use.
-   **Library Terms of Use** — open the license file that comes with each of your installed libraries. It sets out how you're allowed to use the sounds.
-   **Share Feedback** — send a message to the developers, such as a bug report or an idea. See [Share feedback](/docs/beta/support/error-reporting#share-feedback).
-   **Legacy Parameters** — controls kept from older versions of Floe so that projects made with them still sound the same. You only need this window if a control shows a yellow badge. See [Legacy Parameters](/docs/beta/reference/legacy-parameters).
-   **Library Developer Tools** — tools for people making their own sample libraries for Floe. See [Library Development](/docs/beta/develop/develop-libraries).

-   **Add Mirage Folders** — add the library and preset folders of Mirage, Floe's predecessor, if you had it installed. Not shown on Linux.

-   **Help** — open Floe's documentation website.

---

# Changelog

> A detailed changelog of all versions of Floe

## 2.0.4

A big update with redesigned browsers, a reworked Distortion effect, a new Limiter and lots of improvements throughout. In summary:

-   Redesigned preset, Instrument and IR browsers, with a new Browse mode that gets you to a library, preset bank, folder or tag in a few clicks. See the [browsers docs](/docs/usage/browsers)
-   Overhauled Distortion effect: 10 new or upgraded types, cleaner sound with 4x oversampling, new Punish and Tilt controls, and Auto Gain to keep the volume steady as you turn up the drive. Existing presets and DAW projects load with the older types, kept as Legacy types
-   New Limiter effect, mainly for the end of the effects chain
-   Faster audio engine, up to 2.5x faster in heavy granular use
-   Granular Share Grains option: shared grains keep the same density however many notes you play, per-voice grains build chords into a dense wash
-   Variation option for granular layers and random LFO shapes, so a preset can repeat the exact same grain scatter or LFO movement on every note or on each key
-   Clearer macros: see macro movement on the filters, EQ, LFO, envelopes and waveform, see a parameter's macro-adjusted value in its popup, and set the 0% and 100% values directly with Edit Range
-   More descriptive tooltips, with values shown straight away on hover
-   Set a default preset for new instances of Floe to open with
-   New displays and meters: a LUFS meter, peak-hold lines, Compressor meters, a High-pass filter graph, and shape previews for Distortion and Bitcrush
-   Redesigned effects switches: bypass, add/remove, and jump to an effect in the rack from one place
-   Smoother, more useful Bit Crush controls
-   Swap layers and macros from their right-click menus
-   LFO Amount as an MPE press and slide target
-   Wider layer Pitch range of ±88 semitones
-   Respond to MIDI panic messages (All Notes Off and All Sound Off)
-   Many smaller improvements and fixes

This release includes all changes listed in the beta changelogs below: 2.0.4-beta.1 through to 2.0.4-beta.3.

### Changes since 2.0.4-beta.3

-   Fix clicks sometimes being ignored when Floe is busy, for example very quick clicks or moving the mouse away straight after clicking
-   Fix notes looping forever when a loop mode is set but the volume envelope is off
-   Fix the arpeggiator's step right-click menu not opening in Overview
-   Fix a granular Harmony interval you've just clicked off still looking on until you move the mouse away
-   Respond to MIDI All Notes Off (CC 123) and All Sound Off (CC 120), so a DAW or controller's panic or stop can silence stuck notes
-   Fix renders sometimes coming out with different random variations (grains, random LFO shapes, the arpeggiator's Humanise and Random orders, and more) depending on your DAW's buffer size, such as between playback and bouncing. Some DAW projects that use these may play a different variation than in earlier versions
-   Make error messages easier to read: short titles, no repeated package names, and no internal source code details
-   Installing a preset bank that doesn't name a default preset now suggests its first preset alphabetically, so a blank Floe opens straight onto something playable
-   Change the granular Harmony "Fifths" preset to a 5th above plus the same note an octave lower, so it reinforces the root rather than adding a 4th. Existing presets and DAW projects keep their intervals
-   Always show User presets in the preset browser, even before you've saved any, so the layout no longer changes as preset banks come and go and it's clear where saved presets go
-   Sort preset banks alphabetically by name in the preset browser, regardless of which folder they're installed in
-   Add a preference to show Floe's default background behind every layer when layers use different libraries, for a calmer, more consistent look on the Layers page
-   Packager: make each library's 'About' document a PDF, so it opens on any computer, and have it point to the library's license file rather than summarise it. Add `--no-about-doc` to leave it out

## 2.0.4-beta.3

-   Show a parameter's macro-adjusted value in its value popup, along with which macros are changing it
-   Add Edit Range to the right-click menu of macro destination knobs: set the parameter's value at 0% and 100% of the macro directly, and hear each end while you adjust it. Moving one end leaves the other where it is, and an option moves the macro so the sound stays as it is now
-   Fix wrapped text such as preset descriptions sometimes starting a line with a full stop, for example when the text contained an ellipsis
-   Fix the per-note markers on a layer's Volume slider ignoring macros, so they now sit at the level you actually hear
-   Add an "All" row to library and preset bank pages in the browsers' new Browse mode (from beta.2), making it clear when the whole collection is shown and giving a quick way back to it from a folder
-   Add Share Grains to granular mode: choose between shared grains, which keep the same grain density however many notes you play, and per-voice grains, where each note adds its own grains and chords build up into a dense wash. New layers start with shared grains, and presets and DAW projects from earlier versions keep per-voice grains so they sound the same
-   Rename the granular and LFO Seed Mode menu to Variation, with options Different on every note, Identical on all notes, and Identical on each key, so it's clearer what each one does
-   Stop the LFO display flipping a random Shape upside down for a negative Amount when Variation is Different on every note, since it sounds the same either way

## 2.0.4-beta.2

### Browsers

The preset, Instrument and IR browsers have been redesigned. See the [browsers docs](/docs/usage/browsers) for a full walkthrough.

#### What's different

-   Add Browse mode, now the default: click through a few short pages to narrow down to a library, preset bank, folder or tag, rather than scanning a long tree of filters. Switch to Filter mode for the previous behaviour
-   Swap the left and right panels: items are now on the left, so they drop down directly beneath the selector you clicked and need less mouse movement
-   Restyle the browsers to feel like a menu rather than a dialog window
-   Keep the selector that opened the browser usable while the browser is open, so its next, previous, randomise and unload buttons replace the browser's duplicate ones
-   Make Favourites narrow the current list rather than act as a separate filter, so you can see just your favourites within a preset bank, for example
-   Make preset search match preset names only, not preset bank or folder names, so results are more precise and predictable

#### Improvements

-   Make the browsers resizable
-   Add a line beneath the items saying what you're looking at, such as "Showing from Abyss preset bank". Click any part of it to undo that narrowing down
-   Make also open the current item's library or preset bank in the right panel in Browse mode, rather than just scrolling to the item
-   Show the current item more reliably when a browser opens
-   Remember your place in Browse mode, so the next new instance of Floe opens the browser there
-   Group preset banks into Factory preset banks and User presets when you have both
-   Rename the preset browser's Libraries section to Libraries used, since it shows presets that use a particular sample library
-   Fix clicking an already-loaded item unloading it. This was easy to do by accident and left the preset blank. To unload, use the on the selector instead

### Other changes

-   Improve performance of the audio engine to be easier on the CPU, up to 2.5x faster in heavy granular use cases
-   Add a seed option to granular layers and random LFO shapes , so a preset can save the exact grain scatter or LFO movement. Choose Fixed for the same pattern on every note, or Fixed Per Key for a repeatable variation on each key
-   Add LFO Amount as an MPE press and slide target, so you can dig into a key to bring in vibrato or tremolo on just that note
-   Add 'Swap with Left/Right' options to the right-click menu of Layers (the instrument selector button) and Macros (the knobs). So that you can reorder them easily. Swapping a layer also migrates the macro assignments so they now point to the new location.
-   Add a display to the Distortion and Bitcrush effects showing a representitive preview of the current shape
-   Improve the Bit Crush effect. Bits and Sample Rate parameter are now smooth and continuous allowing for more granularity. The Bits parameter also now focuses on a more useful range of around 8 to 3 - where most of the audible changes happen. These changes required new parameters and therefore run through our Legacy Parameters system where necessary (loading DAW projects).
-   Add input, gain-reduction and output meters to the compressor effect, showing the level going in, how much it's turning the signal down, and the level coming out - same as the Limiter
-   Add a graph showing the High-pass filter's response, draggable to set the cutoff - now matching what the Convolution Reverb does
-   Improve how granular lines are drawn on the UI - each grain now fades in/out based on their real envelope from the Smooth parameter
-   Improve how waveform instruments are displayed (sine, white noise). Now, the 'play mode', reverse and 'loop mode' controls are hidden, since a waveform has always ignored them anyways. Additionally, the red line voice markers now appear on the waveform display in a more useful way, placed left to right by pitch.
-   Smooth changes to the LFO Amount, so moving or automating it while notes play doesn't step audibly
-   Fix the Ring Mod (44.1k) legacy distortion type modulating 4 times too fast
-   Fix voice persisting in Granular Playback mode even when the playback has finished
-   Fix tooltips persisting when the mouse leaves Floe's window
-   Fix library icons and backgrounds sometimes staying missing until Floe was restarted, when they were requested while libraries were still loading

## 2.0.4-beta.1

### Distortion

Huge improvements to the distortion effect:

-   10 new/upgraded distortion types: more musical and balanced with smooth gain compensation
-   Cleaner sound with 4x oversampling, anti-aliasing and DC offset removal
-   Punish parameter added to push the distortion even further
-   Tilt EQ parameter added to musically shape the tone (deep through to bright)
-   Auto-gain parameter added to legacy distortion types to opt in so the volume level stays steady as you turn the drive up
-   Fully backwards compatible with existing presets and DAW projects - they will load as one of the 'legacy' distortion types. The new algorithms are not directly equivalent to the legacy types. Changing your preset from a legacy type to a newer type has to be done by ear. Some things to keep in mind if doing that: turn on the Auto Gain parameter for an easy win - the Drive knob will have a much more consistent volume level across the whole knob; consider these legacy to modern migration suggestions (but use your ears!): Atan -> Overdrive, Clip -> Hard Clip, Tube Log -> Tape, Tanh (Decimate) -> Tape, Tube Asym3 -> Overdrive (+15% Punish), Sine -> Sine Fold, Raph1 -> Warp, Foldback -> Wavefolder, Rectifier -> Octave, Ring Mod (44.1k) -> Ring Mod.

### Limiter

-   Add a new Limiter effect: a lookahead true-peak brickwall limiter with Gain and Ceiling controls, plus input, gain-reduction and output meters, intended primarily for the end of the effects chain

### Effects switches

Redesign the effects switches, rather than a simple button, they have a few interactions:

-   See and toggle the 'bypass' state by clicking the little rectangle 'light' left of the FX name
-   Click on an active FX name to scroll and flash the FX in the rack, making it much quicker than lots of scrolling, paritcularly when the rack has lots of FX
-   Add/remove the FX using the checkbox on the left rather than clicking the name

### Tooltips

-   Made all tooltips much more descriptive and helpful
-   Split tooltips into two boxes: a control's value appears straight away when hovered (and while dragging), while its description appears in italics after a short pause. Only the description is affected by the 'Show tooltips' preference. A new 'Instant value readouts' preference can be turned off to show the value only after the pause or while dragging
-   When hovering a macro destination knob, it now also displays what the destination parameter will be at macro 0% and 100%, plus its current value. For example when the destination is a volume knob, it might say -60dB to 0dB (now -12.4dB) which means when the macro knob is at 0% this parameter will be -60dB and when it's at 100% it will be 0dB, and it's currently at -12.4dB
-   Increase how long it takes after hovering on a knob that the tooltip appears

### Meters

-   Add a LUFS meter to top panel - useful for getting presets to a similar perceived loudness. Turn it on using the new checkbox on the Preferences panel.
-   Add a peak-hold line to all peak meters: it marks the highest level reached, holds there for a moment, then falls back
-   Change the peak meter ranges and add min/max markers. The top panel meter: -60dB to +10dB becomes -36dB to +6dB with markers every 6dB - allows for more visibility where you need it - closer to 0dB. The layer meters: -60dB to +10dB becomes -60dB to +12dB with markers every 12dB.
-   Make the layer peak meters always green. The yellow/red segments falsely suggest that there's a problem when actually any level is fine for layers.

### UI Behaviour

-   Make the LFO waveform display draggable: drag left or right to change the Time, up or down to change the Amount
-   Show macro modulation on the filters, EQ, LFO, envelopes and waveform. This is done by either showing a faint 'ghost line' or using the existing display elements that now move separately when needed.
-   Macro destination targets on the waveform sit on the handles themselves (loop start, loop end, crossfade) rather than in a column at the right edge
-   Add support controlling a layer's sample start offset with a macro
-   Add right-click on the effects switchboard to 'Tidy FX Order', which groups all the turned-on effects at the top without changing their order
-   Remove the drag-to-change behaviour from most menu controls. It was more annoying than useful: too easy to accidentally change values. Click to open the menu or use the arrow buttons instead. Some of the 'rate' menu still support draggins such as the LFO rate, arpeggiator rate and delay time, where dragging through the values is useful
-   Add ability to drag up/down on filter/EQ nodes to change resonance (for types that don't have a gain control)
-   Improve the responsiveness and feeling of dragging number/knob parameters
-   Make scrollbars clearer and show up/down buttons on them. Clicking the scrollbar channel scrolls a page at a time towards the click (hold to repeat); shift-click jumps straight to that spot

### Default preset

-   Add a default preset: the preset a new instance of Floe opens with. Right-click any preset in the browser to set it, or use the Default Preset row in Preferences > General to set the currently loaded preset or clear the default
-   Preset banks can suggest a default preset with a new `default_preset` key in `floe-preset-bank.ini`. Installing a package containing such a bank applies the suggestion unless you've chosen your own default. If Floe is blank when the install finishes, the preset is loaded there and then; otherwise the install-complete dialogue offers to load it. That dialogue's actions - sending the package file to the trash, loading the default preset - are now optional, with a Done button to close it

### Misc

-   Widen the layer Pitch range from ±36 to ±88 semitones. Existing presets and DAW projects are unaffected: the previous parameter is kept as a legacy parameter
-   Change the icon for performance controls from 'sliders' to 'gauge'. The old icon didn't look very good and was a little confusing due to ambiguity with the Preferences button and that it didn't actually feature any sliders.
-   Standarise displaying Hz or semitones everywhere for filter cutoff parameters. There's a new preference checkbox to pick either which mode you want. When shown in semitones, the value is displayed as a note name (e.g. A3) instead of a plain number.
-   Change the Performance Controls MIDI CC tab icon to a MIDI DIN connector
-   Fix pops in audio when rapidly changing the Modern compressor threshold or ratio, or Vintage compressor Gain
-   Change button text from 'Copy to clipboard' to 'Copy message' or 'Copy error'
-   Add a quick sliding-up animation for the key-range popup below the bottom panel
-   Add preferences and performance controls to the Main Menu as well as icons on the top panel.
-   Improve icons for Mute and Solo buttons
-   Fix the loop crossfade shrinking when quickly dragging the waveform loop region
-   Fix a crash when the host sends a malformed MIDI event
-   Fix buttons not being visible when the path is long on the Preferences window
-   Fix the layer filter getting stuck (sometimes almost silent) when its envelope moves slowly, until the cutoff was nudged

## 2.0.3

-   Add MPE (MIDI Polyphonic Expression) support: enable it in the Performance Controls panel for per-note pitch bend, press (channel pressure) and slide (CC74), and choose what press and slide control on each layer's Config tab. CLAP per-note expressions (pitch, pressure, brightness) are also supported
-   Replace the Instance Config and MIDI CC Assignments panels with a unified Performance Controls panel (top panel, sliders icon): make the current instance settings and MIDI CC mappings the ones new instances start with, and optionally save named profiles bundling them for switching between setups
-   Add a dialog after installing a package offering to send the now-redundant package file to the trash
-   Show velocity markers on the layer volume slider
-   Highlight the recommended button in dialogs with an accent colour, and grey-out buttons that need text input first
-   Add right-click menu and double-click value entry to macro destination knobs, with options to enter, copy, paste, reset and invert the amount
-   Add copy and paste for effects: right-click an effect or the empty space of the FX rack to copy a single effect or the entire rack (all effects, their order and settings) and paste it, including from one preset to another
-   Add the ability to activate multiple encrypted packages at once by loading a single license file
-   Fix newly played notes ignoring the current pitch wheel position until the wheel next moved
-   Fix preferences file becoming blank or truncated: preferences are now written atomically
-   Fix window opening larger than the screen when the saved window size is invalid: window sizes are now always constrained to fit the current display
-   Fix possible crash when a host fires a timer callback without a timer being registered
-   Fix possible crash when loading a library background image with a very large window size
-   Fix possible crash when reading a corrupted or invalid package file: such files are now reported as errors
-   Fix possible crash and broken audio when a host or corrupted preset/DAW project provides invalid parameter values: values are now sanitised
-   Fix possible crash when a host sends an invalid pitch bend message
-   Fix note-off triggered samples playing forever when a loop mode is set: they now always play as one-shots
-   Fix note-off triggered samples not playing under the arpeggiator: each arp step now triggers release samples like a manually played note
-   Fix stuck notes and hanging voices in several cases: using the sustain pedal while notes play on other MIDI channels, releasing the sustain pedal after toggling MPE, and very large bursts of MIDI events
-   Fix instance config reverting to its previously-saved values when a DAW saved and reloaded a project
-   Fix the tempo-synced LFO rate, arpeggiator rate and delay time controls feeling inverted: dragging up or right now speeds them up
-   Fix unnecessary left side gap in macro destination right-click menu

-   UI split into 3 pages: perform, layers, effects
-   Granular synthesis
-   Arpeggiators
-   Visual design improved throughout including displays for filters, EQ, etc.
-   Improved shape of many parameters
-   New LFO shapes
-   New compressor mode
-   Extra band added to EQ
-   EQ added to the FX rack
-   Better settings for MIDI CC setup, and reproducibility
-   Random variation strip for exploring new presets
-   New default background image

This release includes all changes listed through the beta changelogs: 1.2.0-beta.1, and 2.0.0-beta.1 through to 2.0.0-beta.6:

Additionally, this version differs from 2.0.0-beta.6:

-   New background image
-   Show Modern compressor Attack and Release as milliseconds instead of percentage

## 2.0.0-beta.6

-   Preset favourites now survive re-saving and library updates: each preset file carries a stable UUID embedded by Floe at save time, used as the identity for favourites and the "currently loaded" indicator. Older preset files without an embedded UUID continue to work via a content-derived fallback. Existing favourites are migrated automatically.
-   Show the revision number of a library/preset in the browsers, e.g. v1.2.
-   Lua and preset banks: rename `minor_version` to `revision` to better reflect what it means
-   Fix legacy parameters panel 'Modernise all' sometimes not correctly retaining perfect sound compatibility when macros are involved
-   Packager CLI: change shape of JSON output
-   Tweak preset auto-description logic
-   On the PERFORM page, make the library name use the larger font
-   Fix buggy multiline text input like the description box on the Save Preset panel
-   Fix the lowest MIDI velocities mapping slightly too high; velocity 1 now reaches the bottom of the velocity-to-volume curve and the softest velocity layer
-   Add option to abbreviate parameter names in the DAW
-   Packager CLI: include preset\_banks in JSON output

-   Fix recent regression where right-click menu for libraries didn't work
-   File pickers remember the last folder you used across sessions

-   Fix case where voices weren't retriggering when changing instrument/preset
-   Tweak PERFORM page layer layout
-   Fix FX Mix knob not being correct when loading an old preset that has a macro assigned to either Wet or Dry of Convolution, Chorus or Bitcrush FX.

## 2.0.0-beta.2

Our biggest update to date. This follows on from 1.2.0-beta.1; we chose to skip 1.2.0 and jump straight to 2.0.0.

### Major new features

-   Added granular synthesis (including a random detune parameter)
-   Added EQ to effects rack
-   Added arpeggiator
-   GUI: split the single main page into separate Layers, Effects and Perform pages
-   Added perform page with access to common controls and visual display, with 'Vary' random-variation control replaces the old randomise buttons; click-position strip lets you choose how much to vary
-   Original/Modified toggle on Perform page to audition the original vs modified preset
-   7 new LFO shapes: Random Steps, Random Glide, Pluck, Pluck Sharp, Pulse Narrow, Pulse Wide, Trapezoid
-   Effects rack improvements:
    -   Bypass button for each effect
    -   Mix knob for each effect - replacing separate Wet and Dry controls where appropriate. Loading presets that were saved with the separate wet/dry parameters are perfectly re-mapped to the new Mix and Output parameters where necessary. Loading an old DAW project with separate wet/dry actives the _legacy parameters_ system.
    -   Bypass-all and remove-all buttons on the effects panel header
    -   Right-click reset menus on effect headings and switchboard buttons
    -   New EQ effect
    -   Improve Stereo Widen effect with Bass Mono and Balanced modes
    -   New Modern compressor algorithm alongside the original
-   Third EQ band per layer
-   New EQ band types: low-pass, high-pass and notch
-   Visual graphs added for the layer filter, effect filter, EQ, LFO, convolution reverb pre-filter/post-shelf, and delay filter. EQ and filter graphs have draggable nodes for editing.
-   Undo/redo system added
-   Per-layer stereo width knob
-   Copy/paste/reset added throughout the GUI on right-click menus: parameters, EQ bands, layer tabs, macros, envelope background, and curve maps
-   Reproducible playback added. New panel (3-dots menu -> Instance Config) offers features to reset variability in performances so that you can always render the exact same audio from Floe.
-   Added a new MIDI CC Assignments panel (3-dots menu) for viewing and controls your MIDI CC mappings to Floe parameters
-   New default background image
-   Library-provided background images can declare attribution via `floe.set_attribution_requirement`, shown as a subtle credit on the Perform page

### Improvements

-   Improve parameters:
    -   Filter and EQ frequency controls now use logarithmic mapping
    -   Compressor ratio now skews towards more control for ratios nearer 1:1
-   Improved legacy parameter system
    -   Legacy-override params now show a warning badge
    -   Redesigned legacy parameter panel (3-dots menu -> Legacy Parameters)
    -   'Modernise' feature to convert params from legacy to modern
-   Effect filter: new 12dB and 24dB low-pass and high-pass types
-   Layer filter type menu reworked: clearer band-pass names, all-pass removed
-   New menu option to rescan all libraries and presets
-   Auto-generated preset descriptions for presets that have none
-   Quality of life improvements:
    -   'Unload' x-mark button on instrument selector and IR selector to clear the item
    -   'Unload all instruments' button on the layers page
-   Support encrypted packages (`.floe-pkg-enc`) that require a license key to install, with a paste button on the licence key dialog
-   Fix voices from jumping into the loop region if you toggle the 'reversed' mode of a playing voice.
-   GUI: improve browsers panels:
    -   Collections are now expand and collapsible, selecting all items in a collection is now done with a separate 'All' button.
    -   Left panel (filters) is now dark to better differentiate it and make the collections and icons look nicer.
    -   Sections are collapsed by default, but retains the collapse/expand state across Floe sessions.
    -   Fix toggle not working for Favourites button
    -   Use smaller radius corner rounding for tag buttons to match the rest of the UI
    -   Remove 3-dots menu and instead put the filter selection modes (One, AND, OR) at the top of the filters panel.
    -   Remove dividers between filter sections
    -   Remove "Show Primary Filter Section Header" option. Libraries/folders are now always collapsible - more consistent and intuitive.
    -   Expanded keyboard navigation: section headings, library/preset-bank collections, and filter buttons in the left panel are now reachable with the arrow keys and toggled with Enter
-   Library development: removed the ability to add custom tags for instruments/IRs. Only tags from the known set are now allowed. This change allowed for simpler and faster code and enforces standardisation. Non-standard tags are now ignored. [https://floe.audio/docs/develop/tags-and-folders](https://floe.audio/docs/develop/tags-and-folders)
-   Library development: new [`floe-library-inspector` CLI tool](https://floe.audio/docs/beta/develop/develop-libraries#library-inspector) for debugging libraries — dumps the parsed library as JSON or Lua, captures `print()` output, and reports orphan/missing samples
-   Info panel moved from the top of Floe into a menu item within the 3-dots menu.
-   The tabs within a layer have been adjusted: MAIN tab now contains the envelope and the filter, and the old 'Play' tab has been renamed CONFIG.
-   Added ability to reset parameters and groups (try right-clicking on things!) to their default settings OR the settings of the last loaded preset.
-   Lua: add `vignette_intensity` for controlling background image
-   Save and load preset functions now remember the folder that you chose and will use that when you next use the action.
-   LFO: show a warning icon next to the Target label when the selected destination is silent (Filter target with the filter off, or Grain Position target when not in a granular playback mode).
-   macOS: fix keyboard text input not working in some hosts such as Logic Pro, while still letting the host receive its own keyboard shortcuts

## 1.1.1

-   New monophonic mode: latch. The monophonic switch parameter is replaced by a menu with this new option. In latch mode, the note only ends when all notes are released; new key-presses are ignored and the original note continues playing unchanged.
-   GUI: show more decimal points with very slow LFO rates
-   GUI: better icon for 'missing library' on the preset browser
-   Add infrastructure for updating Mirage libraries to backwards-compatible Floe versions of the library. IDs are now used for libraries, instruments and IRs allowing for changing names without breaking backwards compatibility
-   Add 'fluctuating', 'ringing' and 'whining' tags

-   Package installation: add 'keep both' option when user input is required

-   Fix error with displaying presets with many unknown libraries
-   Fix possible hang when installing packages
-   Fix incorrect loop end\_frame when set in Lua as 0

## 0.8.0-beta

First beta release of Floe. This release is feature-complete. We are looking for feedback on the new features and any bugs you find.

-   Add AU (Audio Unit v2) support
-   Brand new instrument browser supporting tags, search, and filtering by library
-   Brand new impulse response browser featuring all the options of the instrument browser
-   Brand new preset browser with tags, search, and filtering by library. Preset metadata is tracked, library information is tracked, file changes are detected, duplicate presets are hidden.
-   New built-in convolution reverb impulse library with 33 impulse responses
-   New save preset dialog with author, description, and tags
-   Fix instrument left/right and randomise buttons
-   Fix instance ID not retaining
-   Fix freeze when trying to resize GUI
-   Fix GUI opening but only ever showing black
-   Fix randomise parameters

Note: we have jumped from 0.0.7 to 0.8.0. This is to signify the change from alpha to beta but also because it wasn't really right in the first place only incrementing by the patch number. To make the jump obvious we start the minor version at 0.8.0 rather than 0.1.0.

## 0.0.7-alpha

The focus of this version has been bug fixes; in particular around loading Mirage libraries and presets.

-   Max voice is increased from 32 to 256 allowing for more complex instruments
-   Show the instrument type on the GUI: single sample, multisample or oscillator waveform
-   Rename 'Dynamics' knob to 'Timbre' and fix its behaviour - for instruments such as Arctic Strings, it can be used to crossfade between different sets of samples.
-   Fix missing code signing on Windows installer resulting in 'Unknown Publisher' warning
-   Fix layer filter type menu being the incorrect width
-   Fix crash when loop points were very close together
-   Improve loop modes on GUI: it's obvious when a loop is built-in or custom, what modes are available for a given instrument, why loop modes are invalid.
-   Add docs about looping
-   Fix sustain pedal incorrectly ending notes

Mirage loading:

-   Fix incorrect loading of Mirage on/off switches - resulting in parameters being on when they should be off
-   Fix incorrect handling of Mirage's 'always loop' instruments
-   Fix incorrect conversion from Mirage's effects to Floe's effects
-   Improve sound matching when loading Mirage presets
-   Fix failure loading some FrozenPlain Squeaky Gate instruments

Library creation:

-   Re-organise the fields for add\_region - grouping better into correct sections and allowing for easier expansion in the future.
-   Sample library region loops now are custom tables with `start_frame`, `end_frame`, `crossfade` and `mode` fields instead of an array.
-   Add `always_loop` and `never_loop` fields to sample library regions allowing for more control over custom loop usage on Floe's GUI.
-   Show an error if there's more than 2 velocity layers that are using 'feathering' mode. We don't support this yet. Same for timbre layers.

## 0.0.6-alpha

-   Add VST3 support
-   Standardise how tags and folders will be used in instruments, presets and impulse responses: [https://floe.audio/develop/tags-and-folders.html](https://floe.audio/develop/tags-and-folders.html)
-   Fix sustain pedal
-   Remove 'retrig CC 64' parameter from layer MIDI. This was mostly a legacy workaround from Mirage. Instead, we just use the typical behaviour that when you play the same note multiple times while holding the sustain pedal, the note plays again - stacking up.
-   Fix package installation crash after removing folders
-   Fix markers staying on ADSR envelope even when sound is silent
-   Fix MIDI transpose causing notes to never stop
-   Fix peak meters dropping to zero unexpectedly
-   Fix not finding Mirage libraries/presets folders

-   Windows: fix unable to use spacebar in text fields due to the host stealing the keypress
-   Fix crash when trying to load or save a preset from file
-   Improve the default background image

## 0.0.4-alpha

Fix crash when opening the preset browser.

## 0.0.3-alpha

Version 0.0.3-alpha is a big step towards a stable release. There's been 250 changed files with 17,898 code additions and 7,634 deletions since the last release.

It's still alpha quality, and CLAP only. But if you're feeling adventurous, we'd love for you to try it out and give us feedback:

-   [Download Floe](https://floe.audio/installation/download-and-install-floe.html)
-   [Download some libraries](https://floe.audio/packages/available-packages.html)
-   [Install libraries](https://floe.audio/packages/install-packages.html)

Error reporting has been a significant focus of this release. We want to be able to fix bugs quickly and make Floe as stable as possible. A part of this is a new a Share Feedback panel on the GUI - please use this!

Floe's website has been filled out a lot too.

New/edited documentation pages:

-   [Floe support for using CC BY libraries](https://floe.audio/usage/attribution.html)
-   [Autosave feature added](https://floe.audio/usage/autosave.html)
-   [New error reports, crash protection, feedback form](https://floe.audio/usage/error-reporting.html)
-   [New uninstaller for Windows](https://floe.audio/installation/uninstalling.html)

### Highlights

-   Add new Info panel featuring info about installed libraries. 'About', 'Metrics' and 'Licenses' have been moved here too instead of being separate panels.
-   Add new Share Feedback panel for submitting bug reports and feature requests
-   Add attribution-required panel which appears when needed with generated copyable text for fulfilling attribution requirements. Synchronised between all instances of Floe. Makes complying with licenses like CC BY easy.
-   Add new fields to the Lua API to support license info and attribution, such as CC BY
-   Add lots of new content to floe.audio
-   Add error reporting. We are now better able to fix bugs. When an error occurs, an anonymous report is sent to us. You can disable this in the preferences. This pairs with the new Share Feedback panel - that form can also be used to report bugs.
-   Add autosave feature, which efficiently saves the current state of Floe at a configurable interval. This is useful for recovering from crashes. Configurable in the preferences.
-   Add a Floe uninstaller for Windows, integrated into Windows' 'Add or Remove Programs' control panel
-   Preferences system is more robust and flexible. Preferences are saved in a small file. It syncs between all instances of Floe - even if the instances are in different processes. Additionally, you can edit the preferences file directly if you want to; the results will be instantly reflected in Floe.
-   Improve window resizing: fixed aspect ratio, correct remembering of previous size, correct keyboard show/hide, resizable to any size within a reasonable range.

### Other changes

-   Add support for packaging and installing MDATA libraries (Mirage)
-   Add tooltips to the preferences GUI
-   Add ability to select multiple packages to install at once
-   Rename 'settings' to 'preferences' everywhere
-   Rename 'Appearance' preferences to 'General' since it's small and can be used for other preferences
-   Make notifications dismiss themselves after a few seconds
-   Fix externally deleted or moved-to-trash libraries not being removed from Floe
-   Fix not installing to the chosen location
-   Fix Windows installer creating nonsense CLAP folder
-   Fix packager adding documents into the actual library rather than the package

## 0.0.2

-   Fix Windows installer crash
-   Don't show a console window with the Windows installer
-   Better logo for Windows installer
-   Remove unnecessary 'Floe Folders' component from macOS installer

## 0.0.1

This is the first release of Floe. It's 'alpha quality' at the moment - there will be bugs and there are a couple of missing features. This release is designed mostly to test our release process.

This release only contains the CLAP plugin. The VST3 and AU plugins will be released soon.

## Mirage

Floe used to be called [Mirage](https://floe.audio/about-the-project/mirage.html). Mirage contained many of the same features seen in Floe v0.0.1. But there are large structural changes, and some new features and improvements:

-   Use multiple different libraries in the same instance.
-   CLAP version added - VST3 and AU coming soon, VST2 support dropped.
-   New installer: offline, no account/download-tickets needed. Libraries are installed separately.
-   Ability for anyone to develop sample libraries using new Lua-based sample library format. The new format features a new system to tag instruments and libraries. Hot-reload library development: changes to a library are instantly applied to Floe.
-   New [comprehensive documentation](https://floe.audio).
-   Floe now can have multiple library and preset folders. It will scan all of them for libraries and presets. This is a much more robust and flexible way to manage assets rather than trying to track individual files.
-   New, robust infrastructure:
    -   Floe settings are saved in a more robust way avoiding issues with permissions/missing files.
    -   Improved default locations for saving libraries and presets to avoid permissions issues.
    -   New format for saving presets and DAW state - smaller and faster than before and allows for more expandability.
-   New settings GUI.
-   Floe packages: a robust way to install libraries and presets. Floe packages are zip files with a particular layout that contain libraries and presets. In the settings of Floe, you can install these packages. It handles all the details of installing/updating libraries and presets. It checks for existing installations and updates them if needed. It even checks if the files of any existing installation have been modified and will ask if you want to replace them. Everything just works as you'd expect.

Technical changes:

-   Huge refactor of the codebase to be more maintainable and expandable. There's still more to be done yet though.
-   New build system using Zig; cross-compilation, dependency management, etc.
-   Comprehensive CI/CD pipeline for testing and creating release builds.
-   New 'sample library server', our system for providing libraries and audio files to Floe in a fast, async way.
